lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Let's start the review of the new events pipeline, I'll walk through the design and then we can poke holes in it.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Producers write to Kafka, a consumer service enriches each event, and a sink writes batches into the warehouse.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Since Kafka guarantees global ordering across all partitions, we don't need to worry about out-of-order events in the sink.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Not quite, ordering is only per partition, so we need to key by account id and make the sink idempotent.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Right. For delivery semantics we're aiming for effectively exactly-once, using idempotent writes in the sink.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: What retention are we planning for the raw topic, and what's the consumer lag alert threshold?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Sam, what do you think about adding backpressure to the enrichment service instead of letting lag build up?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I think that's reasonable, but we should define the SLO first, otherwise we're tuning blind.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Agreed. For failed events we'll route them to a dead-letter queue and alert if it grows.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Someone should write up the replay procedure for the dead-letter queue before launch.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Do we have a target latency? I recall something like five seconds end to end.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I'll check the ADR and confirm the target in the doc by end of day.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Great. Ravi will own the sink idempotency work and finish it next sprint.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: One question for you Sam, can you review the schema registry setup before Thursday?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, I can review it before Thursday.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Wrapping up: keyed partitions, idempotent sink, a dead-letter queue with a replay doc, and an SLO definition before we tune backpressure.

snippets.title: ADR-7 Events pipeline
snippets.text: ADR-7: Raw topic retention is 7 days. Target p95 end-to-end latency is 2 seconds. Consumer lag alert fires at 10,000 messages. Failed events go to a dead-letter queue.

suggestions.content: Kafka only guarantees ordering within a partition, not across partitions.
suggestions.detail: Key by account id to keep per-account order.

suggestions.content: Exactly-once: each event takes effect once even if delivered more than once, achieved here via idempotent writes.
ADR-7: raw topic retention is 7 days; lag alert fires at 10,000 messages.
Backpressure: slowing producers or consumers when downstream cannot keep up.
Dead-letter queue: holds events that failed processing so they can be inspected and replayed.
Write the replay procedure for the dead-letter queue before launch; no owner assigned.
